recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if Financial Management makes a new decision about the relationship between Coverage.order and Account.coverage.priority.
issue_request: FHIR-27106 was a Published / Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core Financial Management change request asking to resolve tension between Coverage.order's definition and coordination-of-benefits requirement by adding an example with several ordered coverages and a use case where only a subset applies as primary/secondary for that use case.
initial_application: No Jira-tagged source commit for FHIR-27106 was found. Current-history commits 720258c80a99566e1259c4c1a1dcacd8fbc5abbf and 9f780149387dc652bec02aa7744e52774acddbc9 added and polished the requested example, while later FHIR-43028 commit 69ee02c04f6590507f2ac9fc4b0d0461e1416ab0 corrected the inherited typo and added the Account.coverage.priority clarification.
additional_context: Coverage is active in source/fhir.ini, making source/coverage/structuredefinition-Coverage.xml build-scope source. FHIR-27107 records the related context distinction between Coverage.order and Account.coverage.priority as a no-change decision, and FHIR-43028 later clarified that Coverage.order is use-case-independent COB ordering while Account.coverage.priority is use-case-dependent; FHIR-43028 is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current Coverage.order definition already includes the FHIR-27106 example and preserves the later FHIR-43028 clarification.

related_jiras.note: Resolved - No Change issue explaining that Coverage.order and Account.coverage.priority have similar ordering purposes but apply in different contexts.
Later Applied issue added the current Coverage.order sentence distinguishing use-case-independent COB order from Account.coverage.priority.
